name: Bulbasaur
location: Starter in Red/Blue; gift in Cerulean City in Yellow.
summary: A calm seed-backed starter that sets the pace with status, leeching, and reliable bulk.
role: Bulbasaur thrives as an early-game control monster, checking water routes and many gym matchups with sleep or poison support.
fieldNote: In Kanto's early journey, Bulbasaur feels like a tactical companion built for steady progress rather than burst damage.

pokedexText.red: A strange seed was planted on its back at birth. The plant sprouts and grows with this POKéMON.
pokedexText.yellow: It can go for days without eating a single morsel. In the bulb on its back, it stores energy.

name: Ivysaur
location: Evolved from Bulbasaur; not found wild in standard play.
summary: The middle form carries stronger grass pressure while still feeling nimble and dependable.
role: Ivysaur acts like a field captain for midgame teams, blending resilience with razor-leaf utility against caves, rockets, and water users.
fieldNote: Ivysaur reads like a sharpened version of the starter plan: durable, methodical, and excellent at attrition.

pokedexText.red: When the bulb on its back grows large, it appears to lose the ability to stand on its hind legs.
pokedexText.yellow: The bulb on its back grows by drawing energy. It gives off an aroma when it is ready to bloom.

name: Venusaur
location: Final evolution from Bulbasaur line.
summary: A huge plant-backed finisher that turns the starter line into a durable endgame anchor.
role: Venusaur dominates long fights, shrugs off chip well, and gives Kanto teams a grounded answer to many watery or earthy threats.
fieldNote: Venusaur feels like living terrain support: heavy, calm, and built to win the long battle.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The plant blooms when it is absorbing solar energy. It stays on the move to seek sunlight.
pokedexText.red: The plant blooms when it is absorbing solar energy. It stays on the move to seek sunlight.
pokedexText.yellow: The flower on its back catches the sun's rays. The sunlight is then absorbed and used for energy.

name: Charmander
location: Starter in Red/Blue; gift on Route 24 in Yellow.
summary: A fragile but explosive fire starter that rewards patience in the earliest routes.
role: Charmander grows from underdog to sweeper, roasting bugs, grasses, and many trainers once its movepool catches up.
fieldNote: Early Kanto makes Charmander work for every win, which gives the whole line a scrappy survivor energy.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Obviously prefers hot places. When it rains, steam is said to spout from the tip of its tail.
pokedexText.yellow: The flame at the tip of its tail makes a sound as it burns. You can only hear it in quiet places.

name: Charmeleon
location: Evolved from Charmander.
summary: The sharper middle stage adds bite and speed to the fire-line identity.
role: Charmeleon pushes aggressive play, forcing momentum through high damage and clean matchup swings into the game's many bug and grass encounters.
fieldNote: Charmeleon is the moment the line stops surviving and starts hunting.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: When it swings its burning tail, it elevates the temperature to unbearably high levels.
pokedexText.yellow: Tough fights could excite this POKéMON. When excited, it may blow out bluish- white flames.

name: Charizard
location: Final evolution from Charmander line.
summary: A flying fire dragon-shaped ace that feels legendary long before the legendary birds arrive.
role: Charizard turns world traversal battles into spectacle, bringing aerial pressure and broad offensive coverage to late-game Kanto.
fieldNote: Charizard is pure poster energy in Red, Blue, and Yellow: fast, dramatic, and built to close a run in style.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Spits fire that is hot enough to melt boulders. Known to cause forest fires unintentionally.
pokedexText.yellow: When expelling a blast of super hot fire, the red flame at the tip of its tail burns more intensely.

name: Squirtle
location: Starter in Red/Blue; gift in Vermilion City in Yellow.
summary: A sturdy water starter with defensive utility and a smooth matchup spread.
role: Squirtle interacts with Kanto as a practical all-rounder, keeping rock and ground threats honest while rarely feeling out of place.
fieldNote: Squirtle gives the opening stretch a stable rhythm and rarely feels like the wrong choice.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: After birth, its back swells and hardens into a shell. Powerfully sprays foam from its mouth.
pokedexText.yellow: Shoots water at prey while in the water. Withdraws into its shell when in danger.

name: Wartortle
location: Evolved from Squirtle.
summary: This middle form hardens the turtle line into a composed and efficient battler.
role: Wartortle functions like a disciplined route cleaner that can absorb hits, punish cave dwellers, and stay relevant in most gyms.
fieldNote: Wartortle has that classic Game Boy mid-evolution feel: dependable, underrated, and always useful.

pokedexText.red: Often hides in water to stalk unwary prey. For swimming fast, it moves its ears to maintain balance.
pokedexText.yellow: When tapped, this POKéMON will pull in its head, but its tail will still stick out a little bit.

name: Blastoise
location: Final evolution from Squirtle line.
summary: A heavy artillery turtle that turns defense into pressure.
role: Blastoise is a battlefield stabilizer in Kanto, strong into many routes and excellent for players who prefer clean, low-risk turns.
fieldNote: Blastoise feels engineered for the cartridge era: compact, tanky, and constantly in control.

pokedexText.red: A brutal POKéMON with pressurized water jets on its shell. They are used for high speed tackles.
pokedexText.yellow: Once it takes aim at its enemy, it blasts out water with even more force than a fire hose.

name: Caterpie
location: Viridian Forest and nearby grass in early Kanto.
summary: A humble forest bug that evolves quickly and teaches momentum.
role: Caterpie's whole role is early transformation: it appears fast, levels fast, and helps new teams reach a useful flier almost immediately.
fieldNote: Caterpie embodies the quick-growth loop that makes the first forest feel alive.

name: Metapod
location: Viridian Forest or evolved from Caterpie.
summary: The cocoon stage slows battle tempo but signals how close the line is to paying off.
role: Metapod mostly interacts with the world as a transition state, soaking a few hits while waiting for the powerful level 10 jump.
fieldNote: Metapod is the cartridge-era promise that a little patience turns weak encounters into something memorable.

name: Butterfree
location: Evolved from Caterpie line; sometimes seen as a route sweeper for early teams.
summary: A fast payoff bug with status utility that matters much longer than people expect.
role: Butterfree influences Kanto through sleep and stun support, making wild catching and early boss fights far easier.
fieldNote: Butterfree plays like an early specialist drone: light frame, wide reach, and great support tools.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: In battle, it flaps its wings at high speed to release highly toxic dust into the air.

name: Weedle
location: Viridian Forest and nearby early routes.
summary: A poisonous early bug line that leans more aggressive than Caterpie's family.
role: Weedle pressures the opening routes through poison chip, reminding players that even tiny forest encounters can shape resource use.
fieldNote: Weedle gives Viridian Forest a little danger and a little chaos.

locations: Kanto Route 2 South Towards Viridian City

name: Kakuna
location: Viridian Forest or evolved from Weedle.
summary: The cocoon stage of the Weedle line waits out danger before the lance-bearing final form appears.
role: Kakuna rarely defines battles on its own, but it marks one of Kanto's fastest early evolution pipelines.
fieldNote: Kakuna is the visual pause before the line pivots into offense.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Almost incapable of moving, this POKéMON can only harden its shell to protect itself from predators.
pokedexText.red: Almost incapable of moving, this POKéMON can only harden its shell to protect itself from predators.
pokedexText.yellow: Able to move only slightly. When endangered, it may stick out its stinger and poison its enemy.

name: Beedrill
location: Evolved from Weedle line.
summary: A sharp, high-pressure bug that brings speed and poisonous threat to the early game.
role: Beedrill interacts with the world as an ambush predator, excelling at quick strikes and making route battles feel more dangerous.
fieldNote: Beedrill feels like the harsher forest outcome: less support, more venom and velocity.

pokedexText.red: Flies at high speed and attacks using its large venomous stingers on its forelegs and tail.
pokedexText.yellow: It has 3 poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.

name: Pidgey
location: Route 1, Route 2, and many early grassy paths.
summary: The default Kanto bird is common because it fits almost any team plan.
role: Pidgey makes the world feel connected; it is always nearby, always usable, and evolves into a reliable travel-era battler.
fieldNote: Few species sell the 'open road' feeling of Kanto more than Pidgey.

locations: Kanto Route 2 South Towards Viridian City
Kanto Route 2 South Towards Viridian City

pokedexText.red: A common sight in forests and woods. It flaps its wings at ground level to kick up blinding sand.
pokedexText.yellow: Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.

name: Pidgeotto
location: Mid-stage bird evolved from Pidgey or encountered by trainers throughout Kanto.
summary: A stronger aerial route partner that keeps flying coverage relevant all game.
role: Pidgeotto patrols the spaces between towns, serving as the face of everyday trainer battles and dependable neutral damage.
fieldNote: Pidgeotto feels like the road-tested upgrade every Kanto trainer recognizes.

pokedexText.red: Very protective of its sprawling territorial area, this POKéMON will fiercely peck at any intruder.
pokedexText.yellow: This POKéMON is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.

name: Pidgeot
location: Final evolution from Pidgey line.
summary: A sleek sky hunter that gives the common bird line a polished endgame identity.
role: Pidgeot interacts with Kanto as a swift aerial finisher, cleaning up grass, bug, and fighting-heavy fights with ease.
fieldNote: Pidgeot turns the most ordinary encounter family into a real flagship.

pokedexText.yellow: This POKéMON flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.

name: Rattata
location: Routes around Pallet, Viridian, and many city edges.
summary: A scrappy scavenger that appears constantly and battles like it has something to prove.
role: Rattata defines the rough edge of early Kanto, chewing through routes with speed and reminding players that common does not mean harmless.
fieldNote: Rattata is tiny, relentless, and absolutely part of the region's street-level texture.

locations: Kanto Route 2 South Towards Viridian City
Kanto Route 2 South Towards Viridian City

name: Raticate
location: Evolved from Rattata or encountered on later routes.
summary: An older, meaner rodent built for fast physical pressure.
role: Raticate operates like a city and route scavenger that can punish unprepared teams with surprisingly hard hits.
fieldNote: Raticate captures that original-games feeling of everyday wildlife turning dangerous in a hurry.

name: Spearow
location: Early routes east of Viridian and many open roads.
summary: A harsher bird than Pidgey, with a more direct and aggressive battle profile.
role: Spearow sweeps across Kanto's open spaces as a sharp, quick attacker that fits offensive teams right away.
fieldNote: Spearow's energy is less peaceful road bird and more noisy territorial interceptor.

pokedexText.red: Eats bugs in grassy areas. It has to flap its short wings at high speed to stay airborne.
pokedexText.yellow: Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its ter­ ritory.

name: Fearow
location: Evolved from Spearow; seen with trainers across Kanto.
summary: A long-beaked sky predator that translates route aggression into real power.
role: Fearow impacts the world as a dive attacker, excellent for fast clears and one of the cartridge era's satisfying practical fliers.
fieldNote: Fearow feels like Kanto's high-speed patrol craft.

pokedexText.yellow: A POKéMON that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.

name: Ekans
location: Routes near Cerulean and cycling corridors; version-favored in Red.
summary: A coiled ambusher that turns ordinary grass patches into threat zones.
role: Ekans interacts with Kanto through poison pressure and territorial behavior, making it a strong symbol of the region's rougher roadside ecology.
fieldNote: Ekans is the kind of encounter that changes how carefully you walk through tall grass.

name: Arbok
location: Evolved from Ekans or used by Team Rocket members.
summary: A larger poison constrictor whose intimidation is part of its value.
role: Arbok reads like an enforcer in Red, Blue, and Yellow, often tied to Rocket-style menace and attrition-based fights.
fieldNote: Arbok adds a genuine criminal-underground flavor to Kanto's encounter table.

pokedexText.yellow: The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.

name: Pikachu
location: Viridian Forest in Red/Blue; starter partner in Yellow.
summary: The mascot mouse is surprisingly scarce in the wild but electric in personality.
role: Pikachu shapes the world through speed, paralysis, and pure icon status, especially in Yellow where it becomes the emotional center of the journey.
evolution: Pichu does not exist in Gen 1; Pikachu -> Raichu by Thunder Stone
fieldNote: Few Pokemon alter the feel of a version the way Pikachu does in Yellow.

name: Raichu
location: Evolved from Pikachu with a Thunder Stone; Lt. Surge's ace is a famous example.
summary: A heavier electric finisher that trades mascot charm for raw discharge power.
role: Raichu energizes the Kanto grid by forcing fast damage races and punishing water or flying targets immediately.
fieldNote: In the original games, Raichu feels like Pikachu's battle-optimized final output.

name: Sandshrew
location: Dry routes and tunnels; version-favored in Blue.
summary: A desert-ready digger that feels built for the harsher side of Kanto's terrain.
role: Sandshrew interacts with the world as a burrowing defender, resisting electric lines and thriving in dusty, rocky spaces.
fieldNote: Sandshrew gives Kanto's open ground a survivalist, armored quality.

name: Sandslash
location: Evolved from Sandshrew or encountered in tougher dry zones.
summary: A clawed burrower that turns grounded defense into offense.
role: Sandslash patrols caves and rough routes as a durable physical threat, especially useful around electric and poison-heavy teams.
fieldNote: Sandslash feels like a sharpened geology lesson with claws.

summary: The female Nidoran line begins as a versatile poison-type with strong long-term upside.
role: Nidoran F influences Kanto through flexible growth, becoming a prized catch because its final form gains broad utility.

name: Nidorina
location: Evolved from Nidoran F.
summary: A tougher middle stage that bridges fast growth and stone evolution power.
role: Nidorina gives players freedom: keep leveling for moves or trigger the Moon Stone route into Nidoqueen when ready.

fieldNote: Nidorina captures the original games' love of flexible evolution timing.

role: Nidoqueen interacts with Kanto like a battlefield tank, handling caves, poison zones, electric threats, and many generic trainer fights smoothly.
evolution: Nidoran F -> Nidorina (Lv16) -> Nidoqueen by Moon Stone
fieldNote: Nidoqueen is one of Gen 1's most practical all-terrain monsters.

name: Nidoran M
location: Route 22 and nearby open fields.
summary: The male Nidoran line grows into one of Kanto's most explosive power builds.
role: Nidoran M affects the world by giving players an early route to huge offensive payoff if they stick with it.
evolution: Nidoran M -> Nidorino (Lv16) -> Nidoking by Moon Stone
fieldNote: From the start, Nidoran M feels wired for aggression.

name: Nidorino
location: Evolved from Nidoran M.

role: Nidorino bridges route-level efficiency and late-game power, often arriving before many rivals fully stabilize.
evolution: Nidoran M -> Nidorino (Lv16) -> Nidoking by Moon Stone
fieldNote: Nidorino has the exact posture of a creature about to become a centerpiece.

summary: A mystical fire fox that adds elegance and status pressure to the region.

fieldNote: Ninetales brings folklore energy into a world otherwise full of roads, labs, and caves.

pokedexText.red: Very smart and very vengeful. Grabbing one of its many tails could result in a 1000-year curse.
pokedexText.yellow: According to an enduring legend, 9 noble saints were united and reincarnated as this POKéMON.

name: Jigglypuff
location: Routes near Mt. Moon and central Kanto.
summary: A round singer known for sleep utility and big eventual bulk.
role: Jigglypuff interacts with the world through song and disruption, making it feel like part performer and part route-side oddity.
fieldNote: Jigglypuff turns simple encounter tables into something playful and weird.

pokedexText.red: When its huge eyes light up, it sings a mysteriously soothing melody that lulls its enemies to sleep.
pokedexText.yellow: Uses its alluring eyes to enrapture its foe. It then sings a pleasing melody that lulls the foe to sleep.

name: Wigglytuff
location: Moon Stone evolution from Jigglypuff.
summary: A sturdier balloon battler whose value comes from range and survivability.
role: Wigglytuff handles Kanto like a broad-coverage normal type that can fill gaps where more specialized monsters are missing.
fieldNote: Wigglytuff feels like cheerful utility wrapped around a very practical statline.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: The body is soft and rubbery. When angered, it will suck in air and inflate itself to an enormous size.
pokedexText.yellow: Its body is full of elasticity. By inhaling deeply, it can continue to inflate itself without limit.

name: Zubat
location: Mt. Moon, Rock Tunnel, Victory Road, and many caves.
summary: The cave bat is everywhere, making darkness feel inhabited and noisy.
role: Zubat's real interaction with Kanto is environmental: it defines cave identity, harassing travelers while embodying underground ecology.
fieldNote: No Pokemon is more synonymous with Gen 1 cave travel than Zubat.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Forms colonies in perpetually dark places. Uses ultrasonic waves to identify and approach targets.
pokedexText.yellow: Emits ultrasonic cries while it flies. They act as a sonar used to check for ob­ jects in its way.

name: Golbat
location: Evolved from Zubat or used by hostile trainers.
summary: A larger cave flyer that takes Zubat's nuisance role and turns it threatening.
role: Golbat appears as a frequent enemy ace in hideouts and caverns, reinforcing Kanto's association between poison, caves, and criminal spaces.
fieldNote: Golbat feels like Kanto's underground air force.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Once it strikes, it will not stop draining energy from the victim even if it gets too heavy to fly.
pokedexText.yellow: It attacks in a stealthy manner, without warning. Its sharp fangs are used to bite and suck blood.

name: Oddish
location: Routes south of Cerulean and grassy city edges; version-favored in Red.
summary: A rooted night-plant that gives the early midgame a practical grass option.
role: Oddish interacts with Kanto as a roadside forager, strong into water users and useful for status-based attrition.
evolution: Oddish -> Gloom (Lv21) -> Vileplume by Leaf Stone
fieldNote: Oddish is one of the region's clearest examples of wild plant life becoming a battle asset.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: During the day, it keeps its face buried in the ground. At night, it wanders around sowing its seeds.
pokedexText.red: During the day, it keeps its face buried in the ground. At night, it wanders around sowing its seeds.
pokedexText.yellow: It may be mistaken for a clump of weeds. If you try to yank it out of the ground, it shrieks horribly.

name: Gloom
location: Evolved from Oddish.
summary: A drooping but dangerous middle stage that brings solid grass poison utility.
role: Gloom lingers in Kanto's routes and gardens like a heavy-scented hazard, wearing teams down with powders and steady damage.
evolution: Oddish -> Gloom (Lv21) -> Vileplume by Leaf Stone
fieldNote: Gloom turns the line's cute root vegetable energy into something more alien.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The fluid that oozes from its mouth isn't drool. It is a nectar that is used to attract prey.
pokedexText.red: The fluid that oozes from its mouth isn't drool. It is a nectar that is used to attract prey.
pokedexText.yellow: Smells incredibly foul! However, around 1 out of 1,000 people enjoy sniffing its nose- bending stink.

name: Vileplume
location: Leaf Stone evolution from Gloom.
summary: A giant bloom whose battlefield role is more menace than beauty.
role: Vileplume controls space with status and durable grass pressure, making it a strong representative of Kanto's toxic plant life.
evolution: Oddish -> Gloom (Lv21) -> Vileplume by Leaf Stone
fieldNote: Vileplume feels like the evolved endpoint of Kanto's overgrown ecology.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
pokedexText.red: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
pokedexText.yellow: Flaps its broad flower petals to scatter its poisonous pollen. The flapping sound is very loud.

name: Paras
location: Mt. Moon and Safari-adjacent spaces.
summary: A mushroom-bearing insect that gives caves a damp, parasitic flavor.
role: Paras interacts with the world through spores and draining attacks, evoking fungal growth spreading through shadowy habitats.
fieldNote: Paras is one of the stranger creatures in Gen 1, equal parts bug encounter and cave fungus.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Burrows to suck tree roots. The mushrooms on its back grow by draw­ ing nutrients from the bug host.
pokedexText.red: Burrows to suck tree roots. The mushrooms on its back grow by draw­ ing nutrients from the bug host.
pokedexText.yellow: Burrows under the ground to gnaw on tree roots. The mushrooms on its back absorb most of the nutrition.

name: Parasect
location: Evolved from Paras or found in the Safari Zone.
summary: A larger fungal host that fights like a walking patch of spores.
role: Parasect changes the feel of encounters by combining sleep or stun options with a creepy ecological story of takeover.
fieldNote: Parasect makes Kanto feel weirder and more biologically uncanny.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: A host-parasite pair in which the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug. Prefers damp places.
pokedexText.red: A host-parasite pair in which the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug. Prefers damp places.
pokedexText.yellow: The bug host is drained of energy by the mushrooms on its back. They appear to do all the thinking.

name: Venonat
location: Safari Zone and grassy late-game routes.
summary: A fuzzy nocturnal bug that sits between nuisance and specialist.
role: Venonat influences Kanto with status-heavy bug poison play, often showing up where the region's marshier or wilder edges take over.
fieldNote: Venonat has the feeling of a sensor drone disguised as an insect.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Lives in the shadows of tall trees where it eats insects. It is attracted by light at night.
pokedexText.red: Lives in the shadows of tall trees where it eats insects. It is attracted by light at night.
pokedexText.yellow: Its large eyes act as radars. In a bright place, you can see that they are clusters of many tiny eyes.

name: Venomoth
location: Evolved from Venonat or seen in the Safari Zone.
summary: A winged venom specialist with strong utility moves.
role: Venomoth drifts through Kanto like a toxic night watcher, bringing powders and bug pressure to drawn-out fights.
fieldNote: Venomoth gives the bug roster a genuinely eerie endgame silhouette.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The dust-like scales covering its wings are color coded to indicate the kinds of poison it has.
pokedexText.red: The dust-like scales covering its wings are color coded to indicate the kinds of poison it has.
pokedexText.yellow: The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.

name: Diglett
location: Diglett's Cave and connected routes.
summary: A small tunnel specialist best known for speed and simple efficiency.
role: Diglett turns Kanto's underground passages into a place where lightning-based teams have to slow down and think.
fieldNote: Diglett's Cave would not feel like Diglett's Cave without the constant sudden pop-ups.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Lives about one yard underground where it feeds on plant roots. It sometimes appears above ground.
pokedexText.red: Lives about one yard underground where it feeds on plant roots. It sometimes appears above ground.
pokedexText.yellow: It prefers dark places. It spends most of its time underground, though it may pop up in caves.

name: Dugtrio
location: Diglett's Cave; sometimes found already evolved.
summary: A triple-head burrower that transforms the line into a serious offensive tool.
role: Dugtrio interacts with the world as one of Kanto's best electric punishers, sprinting through battles with ruthless simplicity.
fieldNote: Dugtrio is the cave ambush turned into a real tactical weapon.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: A team of DIGLETT triplets. It triggers huge earthquakes by burrowing 60 miles underground.
pokedexText.red: A team of DIGLETT triplets. It triggers huge earthquakes by burrowing 60 miles underground.
pokedexText.yellow: A team of triplets that can burrow over 60 MPH. Due to this, some people think it's an earthquake.

name: Meowth
location: Routes near Celadon and urban corridors; version-favored in Blue.
summary: A city cat with quick attacks and a mischievous streak.
role: Meowth gives Kanto's urban spaces personality, fitting naturally around roads, buildings, and Rocket-adjacent encounters.
fieldNote: Meowth makes the world feel less wild and more inhabited.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Adores circular objects. Wanders the streets on a nightly basis to look for dropped loose change.
pokedexText.yellow: Appears to be more active at night. It loves round and shiny things. It can't stop from picking them up.

name: Persian
location: Evolved from Meowth; iconic with Team Rocket leadership.
summary: A sleek predator whose elegance masks real speed and bite.
role: Persian moves through Kanto like upper-crust menace, tying together urban wealth, Rocket aesthetics, and quick physical pressure.
fieldNote: Persian is one of the cleanest examples of Gen 1 using Pokemon design to signal class and attitude.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Although its fur has many admirers, it is tough to raise as a pet because of its fickle meanness.
pokedexText.red: Although its fur has many admirers, it is tough to raise as a pet because of its fickle meanness.
pokedexText.yellow: The gem in its forehead glows on its own! It walks with all the grace and elegance of a proud queen.

name: Psyduck
location: Cerulean-area waterways, Seafoam approaches, and Surf routes.
summary: A confused waterfowl that often looks goofy until it starts landing hits.
role: Psyduck interacts with Kanto as a river and pond dweller that brings unexpected utility once trained.
fieldNote: Psyduck adds a slightly comedic edge to Kanto's watery spaces.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: While lulling its enemies with its vacant look, this wily POKéMON will use psychokinetic powers.
pokedexText.red: While lulling its enemies with its vacant look, this wily POKéMON will use psychokinetic powers.
pokedexText.yellow: Always tormented by headaches. It uses psychic powers, but it is not known if it intends to do so.

name: Golduck
location: Evolved from Psyduck or encountered in later watery areas.
summary: A smoother, stronger swimmer that turns oddity into competence.
role: Golduck moves through Kanto as a versatile aquatic battler, fast enough to feel modern and strong enough to matter.
fieldNote: Golduck gives the line a crisp, athletic finish.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Often seen swim­ ming elegantly by lake shores. It is often mistaken for the Japanese monster, Kappa.
pokedexText.red: Often seen swim­ ming elegantly by lake shores. It is often mistaken for the Japanese monster, Kappa.
pokedexText.yellow: Its slim and long limbs end in broad flippers. They are used for swim­ ming gracefully in lakes.

name: Mankey
location: Routes near Viridian and rocky foothills; version-favored in Red.
summary: A furious primate whose speed and aggression matter early.
role: Mankey interacts with Kanto as a route-side brawler, great for players who want fast physical pressure and anti-normal utility.
fieldNote: Mankey makes Kanto's roadside wildlife feel unpredictable and combative.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Extremely quick to anger. It could be docile one moment then thrashing away the next instant.
pokedexText.yellow: An agile POKéMON that lives in trees. It angers easily and will not hesitate to attack anything.

name: Primeape
location: Evolved from Mankey.
summary: A berserk fighter built for momentum and clean knockouts.
role: Primeape brings raw force to Kanto's trainer battles, especially where normals and rocks are common obstacles.
fieldNote: Primeape is pure cartridge-era rage in motion.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Always furious and tenacious to boot. It will not abandon chasing its quarry until it is caught.
pokedexText.red: Always furious and tenacious to boot. It will not abandon chasing its quarry until it is caught.
pokedexText.yellow: It stops being angry only when nobody else is around. To view this moment is very difficult.

name: Growlithe
location: Routes near Celadon and Cinnabar spaces; version-favored in Red.
summary: A loyal fire dog with balanced offense and a classic stone evolution path.
role: Growlithe roams Kanto's roads like a working companion species, blending dependable fire damage with a heroic vibe.
fieldNote: Growlithe feels like the region's best candidate for an actual trainer partner animal.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.red: Very protective of its territory. It will bark and bite to repel intruders from its space.
pokedexText.yellow: A POKéMON with a friendly nature. However, it will bark fiercely at anything invading its territory.

name: Arcanine
location: Fire Stone evolution from Growlithe.
summary: A massive fire beast often treated like a pseudo-legend in tone.
role: Arcanine crosses Kanto like a noble charger, offering speed, power, and immediate authority in almost any fight.
fieldNote: Arcanine carries one of the most mythic vibes in the original Pokedex.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: A POKéMON that has been admired since the past for its beauty. It runs agilely as if on wings.
pokedexText.red: A POKéMON that has been admired since the past for its beauty. It runs agilely as if on wings.
pokedexText.yellow: A legendary POKé­ MON in China. Many people are charmed by its grace and beauty while running.

name: Poliwag
location: Ponds, rivers, and fishing spots across central Kanto.
summary: A spiral-bellied tadpole that makes every pond feel populated.
role: Poliwag interacts with Kanto through accessible fishing and surfing routes, acting as a flexible aquatic catch with multiple late outcomes.
evolution: Poliwag -> Poliwhirl (Lv25) -> Poliwrath by Water Stone
fieldNote: Poliwag is the heartbeat of Kanto's smaller bodies of water.

pokedexText.red: Its newly grown legs prevent it from running. It appears to prefer swimming than trying to stand.
pokedexText.yellow: The direction of the spiral on the belly differs by area. It is more adept at swimming than walking.

name: Poliwhirl
location: Evolved from Poliwag or available through fishing progression.
summary: An agile middle form that sits comfortably in water-heavy team builds.
role: Poliwhirl feels at home in rivers and city canals alike, giving the line a more capable and expressive battle posture.
evolution: Poliwag -> Poliwhirl (Lv25) -> Poliwrath by Water Stone
fieldNote: Poliwhirl might be the most visually iconic middle evolution in Gen 1.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Capable of living in or out of water. When out of water, it sweats to keep its body slimy.
pokedexText.red: Capable of living in or out of water. When out of water, it sweats to keep its body slimy.
pokedexText.yellow: Under attack, it uses its belly spiral to put the foe to sleep. It then makes its escape.

name: Poliwrath
location: Water Stone evolution from Poliwhirl.
summary: A unique amphibious bruiser that mixes water utility with martial pressure.
role: Poliwrath interacts with Kanto like a river champion, strong into rocks, normals, and other grounded threats that crowd the region.
evolution: Poliwag -> Poliwhirl (Lv25) -> Poliwrath by Water Stone
fieldNote: Poliwrath feels like a swamp guardian trained for combat.

pokedexText.blue: An adept swimmer at both the front crawl and breast stroke. Easily overtakes the best human swimmers.
pokedexText.red: An adept swimmer at both the front crawl and breast stroke. Easily overtakes the best human swimmers.
pokedexText.yellow: Swims powerfully using all the muscles in its body. It can even overtake champion swimmers.

name: Abra
location: Routes near Cerulean and Game Corner prize options.
summary: A teleporting psychic whose wild behavior is more about escape than combat.
role: Abra changes the catch experience itself by threatening to flee instantly, making it one of Kanto's most memorable encounters.
fieldNote: Abra turns a simple grass encounter into a tiny puzzle under pressure.

pokedexText.red: Using its ability to read minds, it will identify impending danger and TELEPORT to safety.
pokedexText.yellow: Sleeps 18 hours a day. If it senses danger, it will teleport itself to safety even as it sleeps.

name: Kadabra
location: Evolved from Abra or seen on strong trainer teams.
summary: An extremely strong psychic middle form that already feels endgame-ready.
role: Kadabra dominates Kanto's battle ecology because Gen 1 psychic types are overwhelming and few foes can answer them well.
fieldNote: Kadabra is one of the most famous examples of an overperforming mid-stage evolution.

pokedexText.red: It emits special alpha waves from its body that induce headaches just by being close by.
pokedexText.yellow: Many odd things happen if this POKéMON is close by. For example, it makes clocks run backwards.

name: Alakazam
location: Trade evolution from Kadabra.
summary: A glass-cannon mastermind with top-tier special offense and speed.
role: Alakazam bends the Kanto metagame around itself, blasting through many trainers and shrinking the value of slower teams.
fieldNote: In link-cable terms, Alakazam is the reward for finishing one of Kanto's strongest growth lines.

pokedexText.red: Its brain can out­ perform a super­ computer. Its intelligence quotient is said to be 5,000.
pokedexText.yellow: A POKéMON that can memorize anything. It never forgets what it learns-- that's why this POKéMON is smart.

name: Machop
location: Rock Tunnel, Victory Road, and trade options.
summary: A sturdy fighter that looks like it was built out of quarry work.
role: Machop interacts with Kanto as labor force and battle specialist alike, thriving in rocky areas and anti-normal matchups.
fieldNote: Machop makes the world feel industrial, muscular, and hands-on.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Loves to build its muscles. It trains in all styles of martial arts to become even stronger.
pokedexText.red: Loves to build its muscles. It trains in all styles of martial arts to become even stronger.
pokedexText.yellow: Very powerful in spite of its small size. Its mastery of many types of martial arts makes it very tough.

name: Machoke
location: Evolved from Machop or seen with black belts and strong trainers.
summary: A bigger combat worker that turns the line's raw strength into serious reliability.
role: Machoke feels native to tunnels, gyms, and construction-heavy spaces, connecting Kanto's human world with its battling ecology.
fieldNote: Machoke is the practical, heavy-duty core of the line.

pokedexText.red: Its muscular body is so powerful, it must wear a power save belt to be able to regulate its motions.
pokedexText.yellow: The belt around its waist holds back its energy. Without it, this POKéMON would be unstoppable.

name: Machamp
location: Trade evolution from Machoke.
summary: A four-armed powerhouse that represents the peak of pure physical fighting in Kanto.
role: Machamp crashes through the region's normal and rock roadblocks, and its link-trade requirement makes it feel prestigious.
fieldNote: Machamp feels like a secret boss-grade evolution hiding behind a cable.

pokedexText.blue: Using its heavy muscles, it throws powerful punches that can send the victim clear over the horizon.
pokedexText.red: Using its heavy muscles, it throws powerful punches that can send the victim clear over the horizon.
pokedexText.yellow: One arm alone can move mountains. Using all four arms, this POKéMON fires off awesome punches.

name: Bellsprout
location: Routes south of Cerulean and central grasslands; version-favored in Blue.
summary: A lanky carnivorous plant that serves as Blue's roadside grass counterpart.
role: Bellsprout gives Kanto another aggressive plant presence, threatening with wraps, powders, and type pressure into water or ground foes.
evolution: Bellsprout -> Weepinbell (Lv21) -> Victreebel by Leaf Stone
fieldNote: Bellsprout always feels a little stranger and more predatory than it first appears.

pokedexText.red: A carnivorous POKéMON that traps and eats bugs. It uses its root feet to soak up needed moisture.
pokedexText.yellow: Prefers hot and humid places. It ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them.

name: Weepinbell
location: Evolved from Bellsprout.
summary: A hanging pitcher plant that turns the line's weirdness into menace.
role: Weepinbell influences Kanto through trapping and status play, making overgrown routes feel more hostile.
evolution: Bellsprout -> Weepinbell (Lv21) -> Victreebel by Leaf Stone
fieldNote: Weepinbell is a perfect example of the original art direction embracing weird biology.

pokedexText.red: It spits out POISONPOWDER to immobilize the enemy and then finishes it with a spray of ACID.
pokedexText.yellow: When hungry, it swallows anything that moves. Its hapless prey is melted inside by strong acids.

name: Victreebel
location: Leaf Stone evolution from Weepinbell.
summary: A giant carnivorous plant that plays like a jungle hazard with HP.
role: Victreebel interacts with the world as a toxic apex plant, strong in drawn-out fights and thematically tied to dense, overgrown Kanto spaces.
evolution: Bellsprout -> Weepinbell (Lv21) -> Victreebel by Leaf Stone
fieldNote: Victreebel looks like a warning sign pretending to be wildlife.

pokedexText.red: Said to live in huge colonies deep in jungles, although no one has ever returned from there.
pokedexText.yellow: Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is melted in a day, bones and all.

name: Tentacool

summary: A drifting jellyfish that turns open water travel into a real ecological zone.

fieldNote: Tentacool gives the sea that classic Game Boy feeling of persistent ambient danger.

pokedexText.red: Drifts in shallow seas. Anglers who hook them by accident are often punished by its stinging acid.
pokedexText.yellow: It can sometimes be found all dry and shriveled up on a beach. Toss it back into the sea to revive it.

name: Tentacruel
location: Evolved from Tentacool or encountered on later surf routes.
summary: A larger jelly predator that rules many of Kanto's marine battles.
role: Tentacruel dominates the water routes with speed, bulk, and poison access, making the sea feel genuinely occupied by powerful life.
fieldNote: Tentacruel is one of Kanto's most convincing 'wild ocean boss' species.

pokedexText.yellow: Its 80 tentacles can stretch and contract freely. They wrap around prey and weaken it with poison.

name: Geodude

pokedexText.red: Found in fields and mountains. Mistaking them for boulders, people often step or trip on them.
pokedexText.yellow: Commonly found near mountain trails, etc. If you step on one by accident, it gets angry.

name: Graveler

fieldNote: Graveler is the point where boulder wildlife starts feeling truly intimidating.

name: Golem
location: Trade evolution from Graveler.
summary: A compact boulder tank with huge physical presence.
role: Golem interacts with Kanto like engineered terrain, smashing through weaker foes and anchoring rock-heavy teams with brutal simplicity.
fieldNote: Golem is one of Gen 1's most satisfying 'you traded for this' payoffs.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Its boulder-like body is extremely hard. It can easily withstand dynamite blasts without damage.
pokedexText.red: Its boulder-like body is extremely hard. It can easily withstand dynamite blasts without damage.
pokedexText.yellow: Once it sheds its skin, its body turns tender and whitish. Its hide hardens when it's exposed to air.

name: Ponyta
location: Routes near Cinnabar and open plains in later Kanto.
summary: A fire horse that gives open land a fast, burning silhouette.
role: Ponyta races through Kanto's routes as a pure momentum pick, rewarding players who want speed and straightforward offense.
fieldNote: Ponyta looks like motion even when standing still.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Its hooves are 10 times harder than diamonds. It can trample anything completely flat in little time.
pokedexText.red: Its hooves are 10 times harder than diamonds. It can trample anything completely flat in little time.
pokedexText.yellow: Capable of jumping incredibly high. Its hooves and sturdy legs absorb the impact of a hard landing.

name: Rapidash
location: Evolved from Ponyta.
summary: A blazing cavalry unit that specializes in fast route cleanup.
role: Rapidash interacts with the region as a mobile striker, ideal for clearing grass, bug, and many neutral matchups before opponents can respond.
fieldNote: Rapidash sells the fantasy of a fire mount better than almost anything in Kanto.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Very competitive, this POKéMON will chase anything that moves fast in the hopes of racing it.
pokedexText.red: Very competitive, this POKéMON will chase anything that moves fast in the hopes of racing it.
pokedexText.yellow: Just loves to run. If it sees some­ thing faster than itself, it will give chase at top speed.

name: Slowpoke
location: Seafoam shores, fishing spots, and slow-moving coastlines.
summary: A sleepy coastal creature that masks strong eventual utility.
role: Slowpoke shapes the world through mood more than speed, making shorelines feel calm until its psychic side starts mattering.
fieldNote: Slowpoke is one of Kanto's most character-rich species despite doing almost nothing quickly.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Incredibly slow and dopey. It takes 5 seconds for it to feel pain when under attack.
pokedexText.red: Incredibly slow and dopey. It takes 5 seconds for it to feel pain when under attack.
pokedexText.yellow: Incredibly slow and sluggish. It is quite content to loll about without worrying about the time.

name: Slowbro
location: Evolved from Slowpoke.
summary: A shell-linked psychic tank that turns passivity into staying power.
role: Slowbro interacts with Kanto as a bulky answer to many physical attackers, especially in longer gym and route battles.
fieldNote: Slowbro is the cartoonish concept that somehow becomes serious strategy.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The SHELLDER that is latched onto SLOWPOKE's tail is said to feed on the host's left over scraps.
pokedexText.red: The SHELLDER that is latched onto SLOWPOKE's tail is said to feed on the host's left over scraps.
pokedexText.yellow: Lives lazily by the sea. If the SHELLDER on its tail comes off, it becomes a SLOWPOKE again.

name: Magnemite
location: Power Plant and industrial spaces.
summary: A floating electric machine that makes Kanto's tech zones feel distinct.
role: Magnemite interacts with the world as a literal power-system creature, signaling where modern industry has changed the natural encounter map.
fieldNote: Magnemite is one of the strongest arguments that Kanto is a sci-fi region under the surface.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Uses anti-gravity to stay suspended. Appears without warning and uses THUNDER WAVE and similar moves.
pokedexText.red: Uses anti-gravity to stay suspended. Appears without warning and uses THUNDER WAVE and similar moves.
pokedexText.yellow: It is born with the ability to defy gravity. It floats in air on powerful electro­ magnetic waves.

name: Magneton
location: Power Plant or evolved from Magnemite.
summary: A cluster of magnets that turns industrial energy into battle control.
role: Magneton rules electric spaces and punishes water or flying foes, making the Power Plant feel like a genuine biome rather than a gimmick room.
fieldNote: Magneton has the exact vibe of a malfunctioning but effective machine swarm.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Formed by several MAGNEMITEs linked together. They frequently appear when sunspots flare up.
pokedexText.red: Formed by several MAGNEMITEs linked together. They frequently appear when sunspots flare up.
pokedexText.yellow: Generates strange radio signals. It raises the tem­ perature by 3.6F degrees within 3,300 feet.

name: Farfetch'd
location: Trade-only in in-game exchange.
summary: A rare migratory bird whose value comes from novelty and identity more than raw stats.
role: Farfetch'd interacts with Kanto through one of the game's memorable NPC trades, making it part of the region's social economy.
fieldNote: Farfetch'd feels like a traveler that entered the region through people rather than wild habitat.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The sprig of green onions it holds is its weapon. It is used much like a metal sword.
pokedexText.red: The sprig of green onions it holds is its weapon. It is used much like a metal sword.
pokedexText.yellow: Lives where reedy plants grow. They are rarely seen, so it's thought their numbers are decreasing.

name: Doduo
location: Routes and Safari Zone grasslands.
summary: A two-headed runner that uses land speed more than graceful flight.
role: Doduo gives Kanto a grounded bird identity, sprinting across open spaces and feeling more feral than the Pidgey line.
fieldNote: Doduo always looks like it escaped from a stranger, harsher sub-region.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: A bird that makes up for its poor flying with its fast foot speed. Leaves giant footprints.
pokedexText.red: A bird that makes up for its poor flying with its fast foot speed. Leaves giant footprints.
pokedexText.yellow: Its short wings make flying dif­ ficult. Instead, this POKéMON runs at high speed on developed legs.

name: Dodrio
location: Evolved from Doduo or seen in tougher open areas.
summary: A three-headed route predator with intense offensive energy.
role: Dodrio influences Kanto as one of the region's fastest straightforward attackers, ripping through common encounters with ruthless efficiency.
fieldNote: Dodrio feels like a road encounter that evolved into a stampede.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Uses its three brains to execute complex plans. While two heads sleep, one head stays awake.
pokedexText.red: Uses its three brains to execute complex plans. While two heads sleep, one head stays awake.
pokedexText.yellow: One of DODUO's 2 heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 MPH in prairies.

name: Seel
location: Seafoam Islands and cold coastal waters.
summary: A simple cold-water swimmer that gives Seafoam its gentler side.
role: Seel interacts with Kanto as part of the icy marine ecosystem, offering players a straightforward water line with later ice utility.
fieldNote: Seel makes the frozen coast feel inhabited rather than empty.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The protruding horn on its head is very hard. It is used for bashing through thick ice.
pokedexText.red: The protruding horn on its head is very hard. It is used for bashing through thick ice.
pokedexText.yellow: Loves freezing cold conditions. Relishes swimming in a frigid cli­ mate of around 14F degrees.

name: Dewgong
location: Evolved from Seel or found in Seafoam depths.
summary: A refined sea mammal that blends water stability with valuable ice coverage.
role: Dewgong becomes important in Kanto because ice attacks answer dragons, grasses, and many flying creatures in one slot.
fieldNote: Dewgong feels serene until the matchup chart says otherwise.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Stores thermal energy in its body. Swims at a steady 8 knots even in intensely cold waters.
pokedexText.red: Stores thermal energy in its body. Swims at a steady 8 knots even in intensely cold waters.
pokedexText.yellow: Its entire body is a snowy-white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.

name: Grimer
location: Pokemon Mansion and polluted industrial spaces.
summary: A sludge creature that makes Kanto's abandoned lab spaces feel contaminated.
role: Grimer interacts with the world as environmental fallout turned alive, tying together science, waste, and poison battles.
fieldNote: Grimer is one of Gen 1's clearest warnings about what human infrastructure leaves behind.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Appears in filthy areas. Thrives by sucking up polluted sludge that is pumped out of factories.
pokedexText.red: Appears in filthy areas. Thrives by sucking up polluted sludge that is pumped out of factories.
pokedexText.yellow: Made of hardened sludge. It smells too putrid to touch. Even weeds won't grow in its path.

name: Muk
location: Evolved from Grimer or found in the Mansion.
summary: A larger mass of living waste that fights with sheer persistence.
role: Muk turns toxic industrial residue into a tanky battlefield presence, especially useful in attrition-heavy fights.
fieldNote: Muk makes Cinnabar's ruined science spaces feel dirtier and more dangerous.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Thickly covered with a filthy, vile sludge. It is so toxic, even its footprints contain poison.
pokedexText.red: Thickly covered with a filthy, vile sludge. It is so toxic, even its footprints contain poison.
pokedexText.yellow: Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration, it lost its sense of smell.

name: Shellder
location: Fishing and surfing around coasts and harbors.
summary: A shellfish that anchors many of Kanto's marine encounter tables.
role: Shellder interacts with the world as a hardy coastal catch, common enough to feel native but strong enough to matter later.
fieldNote: Shellder is a tiny reminder that Kanto's coastline is full of armored life.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.
pokedexText.red: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.
pokedexText.yellow: The shell can withstand any attack. However, when it is open, the tender body is exposed.

name: Cloyster
location: Water Stone evolution from Shellder.
summary: A brutal shell fortress with high defense and strong ice utility.
role: Cloyster shapes battles through extreme physical bulk and valuable late-game matchups, especially around dragons and birds.
fieldNote: Cloyster feels like a naval mine that learned to battle.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: When attacked, it launches its horns in quick volleys. Its innards have never been seen.
pokedexText.red: When attacked, it launches its horns in quick volleys. Its innards have never been seen.
pokedexText.yellow: For protection, it uses its harder- than-diamonds shell. It also shoots spikes from the shell.

name: Gastly
location: Pokemon Tower and haunted spaces in Lavender Town.
summary: A drifting spirit-gas creature that gives Kanto real supernatural texture.
role: Gastly transforms Lavender Tower from a dungeon into a haunting, making ghost encounters one of the region's strongest mood shifts.
fieldNote: Gastly is the point where Kanto stops being only science fiction and becomes a ghost story too.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Almost invisible, this gaseous POKéMON cloaks the target and puts it to sleep without notice.
pokedexText.red: Almost invisible, this gaseous POKéMON cloaks the target and puts it to sleep without notice.
pokedexText.yellow: Said to appear in decrepit, deserted buildings. It has no real shape as it appears to be made of a gas.

name: Haunter
location: Pokemon Tower or evolved from Gastly.
summary: A floating specter with stronger claws and a louder haunting presence.
role: Haunter interacts with the world as a mischievous tower predator, reinforcing the eerie identity of Lavender and nighttime routes.
fieldNote: Haunter is all atmosphere: grin, hands, and trouble.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Because of its ability to slip through block walls, it is said to be from an­ other dimension.
pokedexText.red: Because of its ability to slip through block walls, it is said to be from an­ other dimension.
pokedexText.yellow: By licking, it saps the victim's life. It causes shaking that won't stop until the victim's demise.

name: Gengar
location: Trade evolution from Haunter.
summary: An elite ghost whose speed and special power make it one of Kanto's coolest prizes.
role: Gengar warps Kanto's battle rhythm with tricky immunities and heavy damage, though Gen 1's ghost mechanics are famously odd.
fieldNote: Gengar is the classic link-cable legend hiding in plain sight.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Under a full moon, this POKéMON likes to mimic the shadows of people and laugh at their fright.
pokedexText.red: Under a full moon, this POKéMON likes to mimic the shadows of people and laugh at their fright.
pokedexText.yellow: A GENGAR is close by if you feel a sudden chill. It may be trying to lay a curse on you.

name: Onix
location: Rock Tunnel, Victory Road, and Gym leader use.
summary: A giant stone serpent that makes caves feel truly massive.
role: Onix interacts with Kanto as moving geology, more iconic in the world than it is overwhelming in raw stats.
fieldNote: Even when it is not the strongest battler, Onix sells scale better than almost anything else.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: As it grows, the stone portions of its body harden to become similar to a diamond, but colored black.
pokedexText.red: As it grows, the stone portions of its body harden to become similar to a diamond, but colored black.
pokedexText.yellow: Burrows at high speed in search of food. The tunnels it leaves are used as homes by DIGLETTs.

name: Drowzee
location: Routes around Vermilion and city outskirts.
summary: A dream-eating psychic that adds strangeness to ordinary roads.
role: Drowzee interacts with Kanto through sleep, hypnosis, and a quietly unsettling urban presence.
fieldNote: Drowzee feels like a rumor from a suburb that turned out to be real.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Puts enemies to sleep then eats their dreams. Occasionally gets sick from eating bad dreams.
pokedexText.red: Puts enemies to sleep then eats their dreams. Occasionally gets sick from eating bad dreams.
pokedexText.yellow: If you sleep by it all the time, it will sometimes show you dreams it has eaten in the past.

name: Hypno
location: Evolved from Drowzee or seen on stronger trainers.
summary: A pendulum-wielding psychic with serious control potential.
role: Hypno shapes Kanto battles through sleep setups and special offense, thriving in trainer fights where tempo matters.
fieldNote: Hypno gives the roadside psychic line a genuinely creepy maturity.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: When it locks eyes with an enemy, it will use a mix of PSI moves such as HYPNOSIS and CONFUSION.
pokedexText.red: When it locks eyes with an enemy, it will use a mix of PSI moves such as HYPNOSIS and CONFUSION.
pokedexText.yellow: Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.

name: Krabby
location: Fishing spots and shoreline waters.
summary: A coastal crab whose straightforward style fits the original games well.
role: Krabby interacts with Kanto as practical shoreline wildlife, common enough to catch and strong enough to evolve into a real hitter.
fieldNote: Krabby adds texture to docks, beaches, and all the little edges of the sea.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Its pincers are not only powerful weapons, they are used for balance when walking sideways.
pokedexText.red: Its pincers are not only powerful weapons, they are used for balance when walking sideways.
pokedexText.yellow: Its pincers are superb weapons. They sometimes break off during battle, but they grow back fast.

name: Kingler
location: Evolved from Krabby.
summary: A giant-clawed crab that converts simple coastal life into heavy offense.
role: Kingler's place in Kanto is as a surprising physical water attacker, well suited to crushing ordinary route foes.
fieldNote: Kingler feels like a dockside catch that turned into industrial machinery.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The large pincer has 10000 hp of crushing power. However, its huge size makes it unwieldy to use.
pokedexText.red: The large pincer has 10000 hp of crushing power. However, its huge size makes it unwieldy to use.
pokedexText.yellow: One claw grew massively and as hard as steel. It has 10,000-HP strength. However, it is too heavy.

name: Voltorb
location: Power Plant, Silph-like tech spaces, and item-trap flavor.
summary: A mimic-like electric orb that blurs the line between item and creature.
role: Voltorb changes how players read the environment, making technology hubs feel unstable and full of booby traps.
fieldNote: Voltorb is one of Gen 1's best pieces of environmental game design.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Usually found in power plants. Easily mistaken for a POKé BALL, they have zapped many people.
pokedexText.red: Usually found in power plants. Easily mistaken for a POKé BALL, they have zapped many people.
pokedexText.yellow: It is said to camouflage itself as a POKé BALL. It will self-destruct with very little stimulus.

name: Electrode
location: Power Plant or evolved from Voltorb.
summary: A hyperfast electric sphere famous for explosive behavior.
role: Electrode interacts with Kanto as a walking hazard, forcing quick decisions and punishing careless turns with speed or self-destruction.
fieldNote: Electrode is the original games at their most gleefully chaotic.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: It stores electric energy under very high pressure. It often explodes with little or no provocation.
pokedexText.red: It stores electric energy under very high pressure. It often explodes with little or no provocation.
pokedexText.yellow: Stores electrical energy inside its body. Even the slightest shock could trigger a huge explosion.

name: Exeggcute
location: Safari Zone and select late grassy zones.
summary: A bizarre seed cluster that turns plant life into psychic life.
role: Exeggcute shapes the world by making the Safari Zone feel exotic and biologically strange, not just expansive.
fieldNote: Exeggcute is pure original-Pokedex weirdness.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Often mistaken for eggs. When disturbed, they quickly gather and attack in swarms.
pokedexText.red: Often mistaken for eggs. When disturbed, they quickly gather and attack in swarms.
pokedexText.yellow: The heads attract each other and spin around. There must be 6 heads for it to maintain balance.

name: Exeggutor
location: Leaf Stone evolution from Exeggcute.
summary: A towering tropical psychic tree that brings huge special presence.
role: Exeggutor interacts with Kanto as one of the region's strongest plant minds, dominating water and ground foes while looking unlike anything else.
fieldNote: Exeggutor feels like a Safari Zone anomaly that escaped into the meta.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Legend has it that on rare occasions, one of its heads will drop off and continue on as an EXEGGCUTE.
pokedexText.red: Legend has it that on rare occasions, one of its heads will drop off and continue on as an EXEGGCUTE.
pokedexText.yellow: Its cries are very noisy. This is because each of the 3 heads thinks about whatever it likes.

name: Cubone
location: Pokemon Tower and lonely ground-heavy spaces.
summary: A masked orphan figure whose lore gives Lavender Town even more emotional weight.
role: Cubone turns Kanto's worldbuilding inward, linking battle encounters to grief, memory, and the mortality themes around Pokemon Tower.
fieldNote: Cubone is one of the reasons Gen 1 feels stranger and sadder than people remember.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Because it never removes its skull helmet, no one has ever seen this POKéMON's real face.
pokedexText.red: Because it never removes its skull helmet, no one has ever seen this POKéMON's real face.
pokedexText.yellow: Wears the skull of its deceased mother. Its cries echo inside the skull and come out as a sad melody.

name: Marowak
location: Evolved from Cubone; one ghostly Marowak drives Lavender's story.
summary: A bone-wielding ground fighter that carries a tragic narrative shadow.
role: Marowak interacts with Kanto through both battle utility and story significance, making it more memorable than many stronger species.
fieldNote: Marowak is where world lore and encounter design fully lock together.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The bone it holds is its key weapon. It throws the bone skillfully like a boomerang to KO targets.
pokedexText.red: The bone it holds is its key weapon. It throws the bone skillfully like a boomerang to KO targets.
pokedexText.yellow: Small and weak, this POKéMON is adept with its bone club. It has grown more vicious over the ages.

name: Hitmonlee
location: Gift choice from the Saffron Fighting Dojo.
summary: A kicking specialist awarded rather than caught in the wild.
role: Hitmonlee's role in Kanto is tied to martial culture and city institutions, reinforcing that not every species enters the team through nature.
evolution: Tyrogue does not exist in Gen 1; no evolution in Gen 1
fieldNote: Hitmonlee feels like a trophy and a training-school graduate at the same time.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: When in a hurry, its legs lengthen progressively. It runs smoothly with extra long, loping strides.
pokedexText.red: When in a hurry, its legs lengthen progressively. It runs smoothly with extra long, loping strides.
pokedexText.yellow: When kicking, the sole of its foot turns as hard as a diamond on im­ pact and destroys its enemy.

name: Hitmonchan
location: Gift choice from the Saffron Fighting Dojo.
summary: A boxing specialist that offers an alternate dojo reward path.
role: Hitmonchan interacts with the world as a cultural artifact of Saffron's fighting tradition, more disciplined than wild fighting types.
evolution: Tyrogue does not exist in Gen 1; no evolution in Gen 1
fieldNote: Hitmonchan gives Kanto a distinctly human-trained combat aesthetic.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: While apparently doing nothing, it fires punches in lightning fast volleys that are impossible to see.
pokedexText.red: While apparently doing nothing, it fires punches in lightning fast volleys that are impossible to see.
pokedexText.yellow: Punches in cork­ screw fashion. It can punch its way through a concrete wall in the same way as a drill.

name: Lickitung
location: In-game trade acquisition.
summary: A rare oddball normal type best known for flavor and novelty.
role: Lickitung affects Kanto more through personality than dominance, showing how trades can surface species the wild map barely offers.
fieldNote: Lickitung is one of the best reminders that the original Pokedex loves weird creatures.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Its tongue can be extended like a chameleon's. It leaves a tingling sensation when it licks enemies.
pokedexText.red: Its tongue can be extended like a chameleon's. It leaves a tingling sensation when it licks enemies.
pokedexText.yellow: Its tongue spans almost 7 feet and moves more freely than its forelegs. Its licks can cause paralysis.

name: Koffing
location: Pokemon Mansion and industrial-poison zones.
summary: A floating toxic mine that pairs naturally with factory and hideout spaces.
role: Koffing interacts with Kanto as airborne pollution, reinforcing the region's science-gone-wrong and criminal-tech atmosphere.
fieldNote: Koffing turns contaminated air into a living encounter type.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Because it stores several kinds of toxic gases in its body, it is prone to exploding without warning.
pokedexText.red: Because it stores several kinds of toxic gases in its body, it is prone to exploding without warning.
pokedexText.yellow: In hot places, its internal gases could expand and explode without any warning. Be very careful!

name: Weezing
location: Evolved from Koffing or used by Team Rocket.
summary: A twin-body smog tank that thrives in dirty, enclosed battle spaces.
role: Weezing shapes Kanto through poison pressure and high durability, especially in Rocket fights and ruined laboratories.
fieldNote: Weezing feels like an industrial accident that learned tactics.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Where two kinds of poison gases meet, 2 KOFFINGs can fuse into a WEEZING over many years.
pokedexText.red: Where two kinds of poison gases meet, 2 KOFFINGs can fuse into a WEEZING over many years.
pokedexText.yellow: It lives and grows by absorbing dust, germs and poison gases that are contained in toxic waste and garbage.

name: Rhyhorn
location: Safari Zone plains and rocky sections.
summary: A charging rhino that gives the Safari Zone genuine physical danger.
role: Rhyhorn interacts with Kanto as heavy safari wildlife, strong, stubborn, and emblematic of untamed open land.
fieldNote: Rhyhorn is the kind of encounter that makes the Safari Zone feel larger than a zoo.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Its massive bones are 1000 times harder than human bones. It can easily knock a trailer flying.
pokedexText.red: Its massive bones are 1000 times harder than human bones. It can easily knock a trailer flying.
pokedexText.yellow: A POKéMON with a one-track mind. Once it charges, it won't stop running until it falls asleep.

name: Rhydon
location: Evolved from Rhyhorn or late-game trainer ace.
summary: A famous horned powerhouse and one of the original game's signature heavy hitters.
role: Rhydon moves through Kanto like armored machinery, smashing through routes and standing out as an apex non-legendary bruiser.
fieldNote: Rhydon has prototype energy in the best way: foundational, rough, and iconic.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3,600 degrees.
pokedexText.red: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3,600 degrees.
pokedexText.yellow: Walks on its hind legs. Shows signs of intelligence. Its armor-like hide even repels molten lava.

name: Chansey
location: Very rare in the Safari Zone.
summary: A healing-focused rarity whose low encounter rate makes it feel almost mythical.
role: Chansey changes the feeling of the Safari Zone by adding one of Kanto's most famous rare spawns, linked to support and care rather than violence.
fieldNote: Seeing Chansey in the wild feels like stumbling into a rumor.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: A rare and elusive POKéMON that is said to bring happiness to those who manage to get it.
pokedexText.red: A rare and elusive POKéMON that is said to bring happiness to those who manage to get it.
pokedexText.yellow: A gentle and kind­ hearted POKéMON that shares its nutritious eggs if it sees an injured POKéMON.

name: Tangela
location: Route 21 and selected overgrown edges of Kanto.
summary: A vine mass that looks like living undergrowth stepped into battle.
role: Tangela interacts with Kanto through entangling plant identity, making remote grass patches feel older and less domesticated.
fieldNote: Tangela looks like the map decorations came alive.

reference.locationFallback: Gift, trade, evolution, fossil revival, or special event only.

pokedexText.blue: The whole body is swathed with wide vines that are similar to sea­ weed. Its vines shake as it walks.
pokedexText.red: The whole body is swathed with wide vines that are similar to sea­ weed. Its vines shake as it walks.
pokedexText.yellow: Its identity is obscured by masses of thick, blue vines. The vines are said to never stop growing.

name: Kangaskhan
location: Rare Safari Zone encounter.
summary: A protective marsupial giant that stands out as safari megafauna.
role: Kangaskhan gives Kanto a sense of larger, rarer land mammals and rewards patient exploration of the Safari Zone.
fieldNote: Kangaskhan makes the Safari Zone feel like a true wildlife reserve.
